question: In covering a distance of 162 km, Abhay takes 6 hours more than Sameer. If Abhay doubles his speed, then he would take 3 hours less than Sameer. Abhay's initial speed is:
solution:
**Given:**

Distance = 162 km

**Formula used:**

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

**Calculations:**

Let Abhay speed = a km/hr and Sameer speed = s km/hr

Abhay takes 6 hr more than Sameer: 162/a − 162/s = 6

If Abhay doubles speed, he takes 3 hr less than Sameer: 162/(2a) = 162/s − 3

⇒ 162/(2a) = 162/s − 3 ⇒ 81/a = 162/s − 3

⇒ From above 162/s = 81/a + 3

⇒ Substitute in first: 162/a &mi
nus; (81/a + 3) = 6

⇒ 162/a − 81/a − 3 = 6

⇒ 81/a = 9

⇒ a = 81 ÷ 9 = 9 km/hr

**∴ Abhay's initial speed = 9 km/hr.**
